title: 科学技術者倫理
subtitle: Science and Engineering Ethics
courseType: Student and Study Skills Courses ProgramCharacter Building CoursesCharacter Building
teachers:
TACHIBANA Tatsuya
授業科目の学習・教育目標
keywords: Professional ethics and codes of ethics
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn ethics is a creative practice to design our conduct by balancing values, not by only observing rules. We will examine social and environmental influences and the role of S&T to comprehend ethical and social responsibilities as a professional engineer (including scientists) in a globalizing society. Upon completing this course, students will be able to improve their ethical decision-making skills for carrying out duties as a professional engineer.
advice:
1.  Overview of this course, linkage between courses, and institutional objectives
2.  Why science and engineering ethics (SEE) is necessary
3.  What is SEE? Why should engineers have special responsibilities?
4.  In what circumstances are engineers required to make ethical decisions?
5.  What values should be emphasized by engineers? Professions and codes of ethics
6.  How to act properly as an engineer: seven-step guide to ethical decision-making
7.  Engineers in institutional contexts: SEE and business ethics
8.  Actual case study
9.  Ethical decision-making practice using the case method
10. The role of engineers in a globalizing society
11. SEE in a globalizing society
12. Ethical issues in specific fields
 - Be interested in news related to S&T to develop an analytical attitude in terms of ethics.
 - Study independently when you encounter unfamiliar terms.
 - With the realization that you are a moral agent in the context of S&T, participate in ethical discussions in class as if you were the person involved in the issues, not a third party or a critic.
books: ACES ed., Science and Engineering Ethics, Hakuto-Shobo, 2017.
requiredKnowledge:
- Review what you have learned from "Japanology (Japan and Japanese)" and "Engineer and Sustainable Society."
- Prepare for in-class group discussions based on your past experiences to ensure that they are constructive.
- Read newspapers closely to be up-to-date with current political, economic, and cultural trends, as well as trends in S&T as a would-be professional engineer.

activityGoals.body: Explain interactions between society (including the economy) and S&T using examples.
Comprehend and explain responsibilities and core values (safety, etc.) as a professional engineer.
Have knowledge of codes of conduct; explain institutional (corporate) activities to promote ethical conduct.
Analyze and consider ethical dilemmas in connection with past experiences and gathered facts.
Not only comprehend the Sseven-step Guide to Ethical Decision Making, but also apply it to actual cases.
Comprehend the LOs of this course and KIT; evaluate your achievements from the perspective of a future engineer.

achievementLevels.ideal:
- Using examples, sufficiently explain the types of ethical problems that engineers can face.
- Persuasively explain to others the necessity of improving skills such as ethical imagination, analysis, and responsibilities.
- Concretely explain codes of ethics and values as well as institutional ethical practices.
- Constructively consider lessons learned from experiencing ethical dilemmas in connection with past experiences.
- Fully understand ethics tests, etc., and sufficiently apply such methods to real cases.

- Explain the types of ethical problems that engineers can face.

- Understand ethics tests, etc., and sufficiently apply such methods to real cases.

              In this course, students will learn ethics is a creative practice to design our conduct by balancing values, not by only observing rules. We will examine social and environmental influences and the role of S&T to comprehend ethical and social responsibilities as a professional engineer (including scientists) in a globalizing society. Upon completing this course, students will be able to improve their ethical decision-making skills for carrying out duties as a professional engineer.

6.  How to act properly as an engineer: seven-step guide to ethical decision-making
7.  Engineers in institutional contexts: SEE and business ethics
8.  Actual case study
9.  Ethical decision-making practice using the case method
10. The role of engineers in a globalizing society
11. SEE in a globalizing society

 - Be interested in news related to S&T to develop an analytical attitude in terms of ethics.
 - Study independently when you encounter unfamiliar terms.
 - With the realization that you are a moral agent in the context of S&T, participate in ethical discussions in class as if you were the person involved in the issues, not a third party or a critic.

- Read newspapers closely to be up-to-date with current political, economic, and cultural trends, as well as trends in S&T as a would-be professional engineer.
